name: \omega = \omega_0 + \alpha t
e: ω = ω₀ + αt is the rotational twin of v = v₀ + at. Use it when α is constant to find how ω grows with time t.

name: \theta = \omega_0 t + \frac{1}{2} \alpha t^2
e: θ = ω₀t + ½αt² matches s = v₀t + ½at². With constant α it gives the angle turned in time t.

name: \omega^2 = \omega_0^2 + 2 \alpha \theta
content: Kinematic equation relating angular velocity, acceleration, and displacement
e: ω² = ω₀² + 2αθ is the analogue of v² = v₀² + 2as. Use it to link ω and θ when time is not known.

name: \bar{\omega} = \frac{\omega + \omega_0}{2}
e: ω̄ = (ω + ω₀)/2 is the average angular velocity. For constant α you just average the start and end values of ω.

name: a = \sqrt{a_C^2 + a_T^2}
e: The resultant acceleration has magnitude |a| = √(a_C² + a_T²). a_C and a_T are perpendicular, so you add them in quadrature, not as ordinary sums.

name: \tan \phi = \frac{a_T}{a_C}
e: The direction of the resultant acceleration satisfies tanφ = a_T/a_C. φ is the angle from a_C toward a, and a larger a_T makes φ larger.

name: a_C = \frac{v^2}{r}
content: Centripetal acceleration in terms of linear velocity
e: a_C = v²/r is centripetal acceleration from linear speed. Larger v raises a_C; larger r lowers it.

name: a_C = r \omega^2
content: Centripetal acceleration in terms of angular velocity
e: a_C = rω² is centripetal acceleration from angular speed. Substituting v = rω into v²/r produces this form.

name: s = r \theta
content: Relation between linear displacement and angular displacement
e: s = rθ links arc length to angular displacement. θ must be in radians, and a larger radius gives a longer arc for the same angle.

name: v = r \omega
content: Relation between linear velocity and angular velocity
e: v = rω links linear speed to angular speed. At the same ω, a particle farther from the axis has a larger v.

name: a_T = r \alpha
content: Relation between tangential acceleration and angular acceleration
e: a_T = rα links tangential acceleration to angular acceleration. At the same α, a larger r means a larger a_T.
